    Arrows of a piece are full edges of the Euler form of its quotients #

    In a piece of the cover, parallel paths have equal composites (ParEq). An arrow is irreducible, so no other path joins its ends: no third point lies on a path from its source to its target (no_mid). For a set T' of points of the piece containing both ends, the corner of the arrow survives in the quotient by the idempotents outside T' (qmap_corner_ne'), and the interval of the arrow in the quotient has two points. Hence the arrow is a full edge of the Euler form of the quotient (eulerForm_c_arrow_quot).
